articleTitle: High accuracy, fully reconfigurable DAQ system for sensing temperature
abstract: The FPGA configurable integrated circuits (ICs) are a valid alternative to the common microcontroller solutions for application-specific (ASIC) embedded applications. The FPGAs are applied in the prototype step, before the ASIC synthesis, for end-user devices targeted to real-time applications. Nowadays IoT solutions with post-processing on cloud-based server technology, makes the dedicated DAQ device an important component in the system. The FPGAs are the appropriate basis for such device, where the data acquisition of analog values and its transfer to digital representation must be achieved with high-speed, high-resolution, low power consumption and effective optimization of the IC resources.

articleTitle: Intuitive Approach to Active Digital Filter Design. Part III: Principle of Higher-order High-pass Filters
abstract: Intuitive engineering is a valuable skill that empowers engineers to effectively tackle problems using straightforward methodologies and simple calculations, rather than relying solely on complex techniques and higher mathematics. Recently, a comprehensive foundation for intuitive active digital filter (ADF) design has been published in a two-part series. Part I introduced the fundamental principles of first-order ADFs, demonstrating their application in designing low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, and band-rejection filters. Part II further explored the design of higher-order low-pass filters (LPFs), serving as a guide for the design strategy of high-pass filters (HPFs). This article continues the series on ADF design by focusing on second and higher-order active HPFs. Similar to Part II, popular filter approximations, such as Bessel, Butterworth, and Chebyshev are discussed and compared to their analog Sallen-Key counterparts. Additionally, second-order active high-pass filtering of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is demonstrated, indicating its better ability to suppress baseline drift from ECG signals.

articleTitle: Intuitive Approach to Active Digital Filter Design. Part IV: Principle of Active Biquads
abstract: The recently developed intuitive approach to active digital filter (ADF) design represents a straightforward and efficient method for designing digital filters. This approach explores the similarity between digital integrators and operational amplifiers in analog filter design. By connecting digital integrators as signal followers, first-order ADFs are implemented. By inserting first-order ADFs into the feedback loop of another ADF, second-order or biquadratic ADFs (biquads) are created. Cascading multiple biquads allows the construction of higher-order filters. This paper, Part IV of the series, focuses on the design of active biquads as fundamental filtering stages in ADF design. A universal biquad architecture, capable of simultaneously generating low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, and band-tejection responses, is introduced and thoroughly examined. Special attention is given to the use of positive feedback as an approach to increase the Q-factor in band-pass biquads. Finally, the application of biquad notch filtering to suppress 50 Hz power-line interference in electrocardiogram signals is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Time Series Salaries Prediction
abstract: The human resource planning is an important task for business management. An important quantitative parameter is the volume of resources, which have to be allocated for the salaries and wages of the personnel. A solution for the estimation of such financial resources can be made by statistical analysis of the past volumes of salaries in the enterprise. The paper makes application of statistical analysis with time series, which are recorded for the historical behavior of the volume of salaries. The forecast of future volumes is performed by the application of autoregressive (AR) and integration with moving average modeling (ARIMA). The paper applies such time series statistical analysis for the case of animal husbandry, in which records are used for three years. The paper makes a comparison between autoregressive AR and ARIMA modeling for the forecast. It has been recommended one of the models, which provides a better approximation between the real and predicted values of the volume of salaries, be applied in the regarded animal husbandry.

articleTitle: Computer-Based Design of Active Second-Order Band-Pass Filters with a Single Voltage-Controlled Voltage Source and a Single-Loop Feedback Modeled by the Sallen–Key Architecture
abstract: The paper presents a methodology for the analysis and synthesis of active second-order band-pass filters with a single Voltage-Controlled Voltage Source (VCVS) and a single-loop feedback modeled by the Sallen-Key architecture. The methodology for the synthesis is implemented in MATLAB. The synthesized filters are investigated in MicroCAP and NI Multisim after choosing standard values of the resistances and capacitances. The material is used in the educational process in the Bachelor’ Course “Communication Circuits” at the University of Ruse “Angel Kanchev”.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv8 Network for Small Objects Detection
abstract: Nowadays, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), also known as drones, are widely used and have gained significant attention in the last decade. Applications of UAVs refer to many fields of people’s lives, such as security, surveillance, and public safety. Computer vision systems in those applications face the problem of tiny object detection. Complex, cluttered backgrounds or infrastructure objects often complicate this problem. An improved YOLOv8 architecture for accurate and robust small object detection is proposed in this paper. The proposed network achieves a 16.3% improvement in mean average precision on the VisDrone dataset compared with baseline YOLOv8 architecture, although it has $\mathbf{4 8. 6\%}$ fewer parameters. An ablation study determining how proposed changes affect a number of the model’s parameters or the model’s precision is conducted. The proposed network and adapting pipeline can be a general solution for a particular small object detection task.

articleTitle: Active Damping of Motor Side Overvoltage in a Three-phase SiC Inverter Based Motor Drive
abstract: Wide-bandgap semiconductors such as SiC MOSFETs and GaN-HEMTs are now replacing Si-IGBTs in the industrial and special applications like traction and air propulsion systems. One of the main problems of direct replacement of an Si-IGBT with a SiC-MOSFET is the high switching speed which results in overvoltage at the motor mains even with short cable connection. The magnitude of the overvoltage can exceed the DC link voltage twice or even more for the cable length of several meters. This overvoltage may result in partial discharge in the motor insulation and fast degradation of it, reducing the lifetime of electrical machines. This paper proposes a commutation method for a three-phase SiC inverter feeding an electrical machine through a long cable. The commutation is done in three steps when the switch is turned on for a short period of time, then switched off, and turned on again. The duration of the first two commutations is selected with respect to the cable length and parameter to cancel the reflecting wave in the cable. The simulation results showed that it is possible to eliminate the overvoltage at the motor side.

articleTitle: Study of asynchronous telecommunication system, based on code division multiple access (CDMA)
abstract: The presented paper is intended to explain to students the main points in the operation of an asynchronous telecommunication system, using code division multiple access (CDMA). The matter discussed in the paper is aimed at the students of the faculty of telecommunications in eighth semester. Some variants of algorithms for obtaining spreading sequences have been developed and applied. In the experiments simulations based on the computer program “octave” have been performed. The students can study the impact of some initial conditions upon the error rate, registered at the output of the receiver.

articleTitle: Naïveve Bayes and Logistic Regression for sentiment analysis and emotion detection from text
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive approach to emotion detection using machine learning by transforming text data into numerical vectors. It standardizes datasets into “Text” and “Label” columns, converting emotions to binary classification. Naïveve Bayes and Logistic Regression were selected, with hyperparameter tuning conducted via GridSearchCV and 5 -fold cross-validation. Naïveve Bayes used alpha and fit_prior parameters, while Logistic Regression used C and solver. Logistic Regression showed robust performance, highlighting the importance of data preprocessing and hyperparameter tuning in enhancing model accuracy.

articleTitle: Application of IoT in the study of biogas release parameters
abstract: This paper describes the development of an IoT device prototype for measuring biogas release parameters. Through the device, measurements are made, and statistics are accumulated based on which calculations are performed. Two types of samples were tested, the obtained results were displayed graphically, and the data was analyzed.

articleTitle: Inventory Modeling for Disbursements Management
abstract: Disbursement management must be done to increase business efficiency. This corresponds to the increase in business profit and/or the decrease in costs in which the business entity operates and produces its outputs. Such disbursement management should be done following a well-defined quantitative model. This research develops such a quantification through the use of relationships that are involved in inventory management. Changing relationships from inventory management enables predictive decisions that recommend redistributing payments through means to increase business profit. The paper derives a suitable optimization problem that estimates the redistribution values of payments. A model predictive approach that exploits this optimization problem is applied. As a result, the redistribution of disbursements allows for the maintenance of the level of payments and/or to increase the efficiency of the business. The empirical application of this business management provides positive results and business results to the ongoing business management of dairy farming.

Author Keywords: model predictive approach for disbursement management

articleTitle: Research of the Influence of Linearly Constrained Spatial Filtering on the Spatial Resolution of an EEG-based Neuroimaging Method for BCI Usage
abstract: The article presents the research of the influence of the size of the region of interest on the spatial resolution of the inverse electroencephalography solution method for use in brain-computer interface systems. Smaller regions of interest are shown to offer higher spatial resolution. The results of peak localization error and spatial deviation computation with variable regions of interest are presented. The results of this work can be beneficial for designing brain-computer interface systems that are based on source localization.

articleTitle: Piezo-photosensitive Device from Fast Green FCF and Rochelle Salt Layers
abstract: In accordance to the current trends for developing sensors that respond simultaneously to several environmental stimuli, a piezo-photosensitive device has been developed. The device is composed of an aluminum substrate on which a piezo layer of Rochelle salt (RS) is electrophoretically deposited. A layer of Fast Green FCF (from solution) was applied on top of the RS layer, and an indium-tin-oxide (ITO) conductive glass was placed on top of it. Separate layers were directly morphologically characterized and a sandwich structure Glass/ITO/Fast Green FCF/RS/Al was electrically characterized under different photo irradiations and mechanical vibrations. Morphological characterization showed inhomogeneous and unevenly distributed crystals and drusen of both Rochelle salt(RS) and Fast Green FCF, on a cracked sublayer. Electrical characterization of the device showed a decrease in current after visible light irradiation. The device has a typical RS single crystal piezo d33 module (max. $212 \mathrm{pC} / \mathrm{N}$) and it showed a significant increase in photocurrent (from nA to $\boldsymbol{\mu A}$) after application of mechanical vibrations. The results show that, based on this structure, new low-cost environmentally friendly piezo photo elements can be developed in the future.

articleTitle: Regarding Artificial Intelligence in Digital Forensic Investigation: Applications and Solutions
abstract: Conducting digital forensic investigations (DFIs) quickly, accurately and efficiently can be accomplished by knowing and using modern technologies, including those typical for machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI). Therefore, the purpose of the paper is to present an exploration regarding the scientific research on the applicability of ML and AI in DFI, how far and in what cases it can support the work of investigators in the different steps of their adopted methodology. A bibliometric analysis is used to outline the general picture and then a discussion regarding relevant articles is performed in detail. The findings show the potential of ML and AI to be used as tools, for example, to improve timeline reconstruction, to find and recover evidence, in secure chain custody, and others. Also, the researchers state that emerging technologies, including ChatGPT must be carefully examined and used in DFI practice.

articleTitle: Investigation of Spray-Coated Titanium Carbide MXene Thin Films and Their Application in Biosensors
abstract: In this study, a water-based eco-friendly solution of Titanium Carbide MXene was ultrasonically spray coated on $\mathrm{Si} / \mathrm{SiO}_{2}$ substrate for the detection of sweat substances. The optimal flow rate of the solution was found to be $0.15 \mathrm{ml} / \mathrm{min}$, and the resulting films had a surface roughness of $\sim 17 \mathrm{~nm}$ and sheet resistance of $156 \Omega /$ sq. Chemoresistive sensors with titanium and aluminum contacts were fabricated and their response to $\left(\mathrm{M g C l}_{2}, \mathrm{N H}_{3}\right.$ and $\left.\mathrm{N a C l}\right)$ was measured. The most stable and strongest response was toward $\mathrm{M g C l}_{2}$ from sensors with Ti contact.

articleTitle: Development and Evaluation of a Novel Marker-Based Tracking System for 3D-Scaled Masonry Models using DeepTag
abstract: This paper presents the development and evaluation of a novel marker-based tracking system leveraging deep learning techniques, i.e., DeepTag, for the monitoring of 3D-scaled masonry models. DeepTag represents a significant advancement over previous methodologies by reducing measurement uncertainty by $42 \%$ and enhancing tracking accuracy with fewer markers. Utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs), DeepTag effectively addresses issues such as occlusions and varying lighting conditions, making it suitable for structural monitoring. The system’s robust performance in tracking deformations and displacements highlights its potential for the preservation and maintenance of masonry structures. Preliminary experimental results underscore the system’s viability as a low-cost and efficient alternative to traditional tracking systems.

articleTitle: Human VS AI-Generated Content: Where to Draw the Line?
abstract: The integration and detection of AI (Artificial Intelligence) in a variety of fields, primarily education, are examined in this paper. With an emphasis on virtual assistants and their uses, it explores the potential and constraints of such technology. A study was conducted with students at the Technical University of Sofia, to assess their ability to distinguish between texts written by humans and AI. The results showcase that learners need to develop their critical analysis skills evidenced by their mixed expertise.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Remote Access Data Recovery Methods: Introducing a Novel Approach and Hardware
abstract: In this paper, a comparison between three remote data recovery methods is reported. The first method is based on commercially available data recovery software, which is one of the best known on the market and has remote access capability, namely R-Studio. The second is by using free Linux software (dd imager command). The third makes use of software developed by Computer Systems (CS), which is based on free Linux software and incorporates a USB version of CSRemoter. CSRemoter is the trade name of a specially designed tool by CS that is used for remote data recovery. The results suggested that the amount of data recovered was higher using the third method. In addition, the third method enabled partial recovery of data from hard disks with hardware damage.

articleTitle: IoT Based Vehicle Tracking System in Smart City Concept
abstract: This paper describes the design and implementation of a smart system for vehicle tracking and monitoring in real time. The platform is based on the application of LoRa technology as a wireless communication infrastructure in the concept of IoT and Smart Cities. Communication requires sending information over a LoRaWAN from the vehicles to gateways, which then transmit it to the control center via the Internet.

articleTitle: Detection of Deepfake Images and Videos Using SVM, CNN, and Hybrid Approaches
abstract: The proliferation of deepfake technology, driven by advancements in artificial intelligence, particularly generative adversarial networks (GANs), has introduced new challenges in verifying the authenticity of multimedia content. Deepfakes can create highly realistic fake images and videos that are difficult to distinguish from real ones, posing significant threats to privacy, security, and information integrity. This study investigates the effectiveness of three machine learning models—Support Vector Machine (SVM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and a combined CNN-SVM approach—in identifying deepfake images and videos. By leveraging a dataset containing both real and computer-generated content, we trained and evaluated each model on their ability to accurately classify these media types.

articleTitle: Micro-credentials design and recognition aspectsoutcome based design with projects examples
abstract: The paper presents some state-of-the-art aspects of micro-credentials design, problems related to their recognition with some examples of open and flexible learning tools developed in projects leaded by the author. Years after introduction of micro-credentials as one of European Union approaches in modernizing the education and training there are still many open issues and problems in understanding and implementing the micro-credential in many countries. Universities also need support in introducing the micro-credential approach in their educational programmes. Last but not least the nowadays modernization of education, including implementation of micro-credentials, is closely related to digitization of learning process and implementation of variety of online tools for open and distance learning. The paper also presents some tools and examples from projects related to the topic, showcasing some approaches for validation of formal, non-formal or informal learning using module-based design of learning content in line with micro-credential approach. One of the often-employed learning modules design includes learning outcomes approach.

articleTitle: Challenges of AI-Driven Cybersecurity
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly transformed the cybersecurity landscape, offering enhanced threat detection, predictive analytics, and automated responses. However, this integration also introduces a range of complex challenges. This abstract explores the multifaceted problems associated with AI-driven cybersecurity, including the susceptibility of AI models to adversarial attacks, inherent vulnerabilities, and ethical concerns related to data privacy and bias. Additionally, it addresses the escalating arms race between cybersecurity professionals and malicious actors employing sophisticated AI techniques. Understanding and mitigating these issues is crucial for effectively leveraging AI’s potential to secure digital environments.

articleTitle: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Hardware Description Languages Education
abstract: The paper presents the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in teaching students hardware description languages (HDLs). These HDLs find applications in various academic disciplines. Different descriptions of basic electronic modules and corresponding testbenches are presented, using multiple implementations of AI. The text (prompt) is given when obtaining the description and testbench, and their simulation shows the correct operation.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of two FPGA-based QRS Detection Implementations
abstract: The following paper presents results from a hardware prototype comparing two different approaches for detecting QRS complexes in an ECG signal - a multiprocessor design and a design with a custom IP accelerator. The research focuses on the parameters execution time, energy consumption and FPGA logic gates utilization. An entry-level FPGA has been used to make the results more applicable for the common use case.

articleTitle: Practical evaluation of intelligent DC-DC fast charger with embedded system applications
abstract: The paper presents the evaluation of an intelligent DC-DC USB fast charger, based on the integrated solution bq25895 from Texas Instruments. The idea is to evaluate the boost mode efficiency from a single cell Li-ION battery and compare it to the stated datasheet parameters. The solution differs from the evaluation board offered by the firm, in sense that the PCB is designed to be as compact as possible for space constrained application. In this sense there will be different thermal performance of the chip, hence this could be a reason for difference in the practical and laboratory evaluation of the solution.

articleTitle: Research and Analysis of the Execution of Different Types of SQL Queries with Impala in Cloudera in Education
abstract: The development of IoT technologies, the drive towards digitization in most spheres of life, the generation of data from sensors and devices in huge volumes makes knowing the tools and techniques for processing and analyzing big data a truly relevant and modern direction. The Hadoop ecosystem combined with Cloudera and its resources provide a powerful environment that is at the same time very suitable for the student learning process. This article describes our experience to provide students with the opportunity to explore different types of queries to different datasets in one of Cloudera’s editors - Impala. The possibilities that the environment provides in real work for conducting the research and the metrics and characteristics that can be compared are described. This research broadens the students’ practical knowledge and gives them the opportunity to try working with big data in a real cluster.

articleTitle: Power Cut Detection Circuit for Embedded Systems
abstract: The following paper presents a new type of a power cut detection circuit using a single MOS transistor. A comparison with existing solutions is done and the proposed circuit has ways to improve some of the parameters of the detection.

articleTitle: Cloud-Based System for Air Quality Monitoring
abstract: Air quality is fundamental to people’s standard of living and health. In recent years, with the development of the Internet of Things concept and of the low cost sensors and microcontrollers, the development a lot of local stations for environmental monitoring has been made possible. This article presents an approach for the design and implementation of a system for monitoring temperature, atmospheric pressure, relative humidity and particulate matter. If more remote sensors modules measuring fine dust particles are placed in different areas of the urban environment, it will be possible to identify the source of pollution.

articleTitle: Black homogeneity temperature dependencies in LCD technologies
abstract: Corner Mura, known as uneven brightness or color variations at the corners of displays, presents a significant obstacle in achieving uniform visual performance and quality. This article introduces a systematic approach to black homogeneity evaluation under higher temperatures, specifically designed for high-contrast automotive clusters. The proposed method combines advanced measuring techniques with both hardware and software improvements to enhance quality across the display surface in representative real-world temperatures. Additionally, it provides a promising solution for optimizing the corner mury, by implementing of aging process. Experimental results validate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Study of the Automatic Emergency Braking Active Safety System of a Passenger Car
abstract: This article reports on a study of the automatic activation of the “Automatic Emergency Braking” (AEB) active safety system. The study includes an experimental determination of the probability of operation of this system in critical situations and determination of the deceleration of a TOYOTA CH-R passenger car, as well as the braking time at different speeds. A modern method for determining the braking delay is presented, using experimental measurements carried out with the non-contact system for measuring speed and braking delay EnergoSM 4.0. The results of the study provide valuable information on the efficiency and reliability of AEB systems, while demonstrating the applicability of new measurement technologies in real-world conditions.

articleTitle: Knowledge-Base for Passive Elements Tools Selection in the Online CADCOM Platform
abstract: The paper deals with the extension for passive elements of the Online-CADCOM platform which offers currently automatic tool selection for analog filters and printed circuit board design. A search for available tools for passive elements is realized and more than 42 tools are selected. Sets of compulsory and optional criteria (tool features) for each type of passive element are defined. For each criterion the set of tools offering the corresponding feature is determined. The information is added to the Knowledge base of the platform, and allows the Expert tool to recommend a set of tools to the user, given a design task. The decision making methods implemented are the Multicriteria Decision Analysis (MCDA), Multi Attribute Utility Theory (MAUT) model and Decision making Matrix.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Analytical System Using Artificial Intelligence for Solving Natural Resource Problems
abstract: The paper deals with the issues of development and research of hyperspectral complexes with automatic system of data processing and analysis using neural networks and photogrammetry method. The results of creation of algorithms for detection of zones of interest and construction of height maps are presented. It is suggested to use geo-referencing of the registered hyperspectral images to improve the accuracy of photogrammetric model formation and determination of spatial coordinates of the search object.

articleTitle: An Unconventional Solution to the Problem of Implementing Three-Input Logic Functions Using 74xx Series Multiplexers
abstract: The paper examines different ways to implement a Boolean function of three variables-through Basis 1 logic gates, through four-input multiplexers, and through cascading of two-input multiplexers. Algorithms are proposed for the implementation of the function in the last two cases in the “unconventional solution”, which will be explained in detail in the paper. The implementation in Logisim of these two cases with integrated circuits of the $\mathbf{7 4 x x}$ series, manufactured by Texas Instruments, is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Variability Modeling for Parameter-based Configurable Software Architectures
abstract: Configurable software architectures reuse common functionalities in numerous software products to reduce total development time and increase product quality. Testing these architectures can become a significant challenge due to the large number of possible configurations and limited testing time. Variability modeling can assist in making intelligent decisions on which combinations to test first, increasing various coverage goals. As opposed to using strict variants of a software module, such high configurability is often achieved by setting various parameters. This paper first studies the Universal Variability Language (UVL) and High-Level Variability Language (HLVL) to assess whether these are eligible for modeling these parameter-based configurable software architectures. Secondly, based on the outcome of this study, we introduce a new variability model language, called Parameter Variability Language (PVL), to better suit the needs for parameter-based variability.

articleTitle: Data Protection in the Field of Automated and Connected Vehicles
abstract: Connected and automated vehicles rely on a set of sensors and cameras as well as on connectivity to function properly and safely. On the other hand, these technologies gather large amounts of personal data. The present article analyzes the legal issues related to processing of such data, its vulnerability to cyberattacks, and the access of regulatory and law enforcement bodies to the data. A brief study of the current legislation is offered and conclusions and proposals on the regulation are made.

articleTitle: Linear scaling GPU enabled simulations of Nano-electronic devices
abstract: This paper presents the development of linear scaling GPU based DFT algorithm applicable to simulation in scales 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup>. The algorithm was implemented as an extension called p-nano to modeling package PINY and was tested with NVIDA GPU from different families with different compute: Kepler - K80, Volta - V100 and Ampere A100.

articleTitle: Using WOKWI Simulator to Support Engineering Student Learning in Microcontrollers and Sensors
abstract: The authors present the use of the Wokwi online environment for the creation of digital content in the disciplines “Microprocessor Technology” and “Microcontroller Programming”, included in the curricula of engineering specialties in higher schools. Simulation models of implemented various microcontroller systems are proposed, including a wide variety of sensors and actuators, LCD displays, communication modules, etc. Simulation models allow the examination, adjustment and diagnostics of hardware, processor software and peripherals. The simulation models implemented in WOKWI provide an opportunity for successful subsequent software and hardware implementation.

articleTitle: Blood pressure monitoring - methods and current trends
abstract: This paper reviews methods and devices that measure blood pressure. Main focus is on non-invasive methods and especially on the increasingly popular cuffless blood pressure measurement technique. Specific approaches and algorithms are presented, which aim to increase the accuracy in measuring blood pressure values, as well as solutions leading to the reduction of discomfort for the user.

articleTitle: A Pure Optical Arrangement Using an Optical Transistor to Form a Temporally Controlled Sequence of Nanosecond Pulses
abstract: We describe and analyse in detail our new approach to developing a simple, purely optical, device for converting continuous laser radiation into a series of nano (or sub-nano) pulses with controllable duration and temporal (and spatial) spacing. The basis is the application of the optical transistor, which we have introduced as an optical device, to control light by light in a purely optical way. In particular, we show the possibility of using a saturable $\mathbf{C r}^{++}:$YAG absorber with its typical manufacturing parameters. The same methodology is possible using saturable dyes as the control medium.

articleTitle: Petri Net Modelling for Energy Efficiency Improvement of a Ship
abstract: The aim is to research and summarize engineering techniques for reduction carbon dioxide produced by vessels in operation. In the article a brief introduction is made regarding the requirements of the International Maritime Organization (IMO), advantages and disadvantages of the described techniques are defined. Petri Net was created to represent ship reconstruction process, and tasks for future research work are set.

articleTitle: Laboratory Bench of a Driver’s Authorization System with Application in Engineering Education
abstract: This study presents the development and application of a laboratory bench for a driver’s authorization system based on components from a Mercedes-Benz W203. The stand includes engine control modules, airbag module, SAM module, instrument panel and electric steering wheel lock, keeping the CAN communication between them. The purpose of the stand is to serve as an educational tool in engineering education, providing students with hands-on experience with real automotive systems and technologies. The research shows that this approach improves students understanding of the complex interactions in modern automotive systems and supports the development of their practical skills. The experimental results from the pilot testing of the system and discussion are shown too.

articleTitle: Current Derivative Measurement Using Isolated Delta-Sigma Modulator
abstract: Most of the control systems operate with the current references which is needed to be realized. The current control strategies are based on conventional proportionalintegral regulators or model predictive control. Both control strategies require knowledge of the motor parameters in the operating point. The easiest way to predict current is to know its instantaneous derivative which can be obtained by the current derivative measurement. This approach is used in the model-free predictive control methods. The current derivative measurement can be performed using existing current sensers and calculating current difference for the specified increment of time or by the hardware solution. The software implementation is much more convenient due to smaller cost of the hardware. This paper is focused on the current measurement using isolated delta-sigma modulator and the data processing of its bitstream to evaluate the current derivative for proper operation of the control system. Several options for differentiating the delta-sigma modulated bitstream was introduced. The proposed measurement system was examined using a model with variable sampling period. The results show that the estimation of the current derivative can be obtained with 10% accuracy in 13 us approximately.

articleTitle: A Semi-Markovian Model of the Spread of Viruses in a Computer System
abstract: In the present work, a security model of a computer system based on semi-Markov processes and the resulting system of Kolmogorov’s differential equations is considered. A study was made of the factors on which the security of the system depends, such as the intensity of infection, recovery, transition from latent to overt form. The proposed model can be further developed and used to model the performance of anti-virus agents.

articleTitle: Optimizing an Embedded System for e-Waste Object Detection
abstract: This article describes how the “Faster Objects More Objects” (FOMO) machine learning algorithm was trained on a new balanced e-waste dataset and deployed on an Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense to localize and classify two types of e-waste devices: computer keyboards and routers. The performance of this system has been optimized and compared to a previously developed embedded system for e-waste image classification. The balanced e-waste dataset and optimized FOMO model have been released under an open license.

articleTitle: Evaluation of High Precision Temperature Sensors
abstract: Developing and evaluating high-precision temperature sensors have significant implications for physical activity monitoring and health assessment. Precision temperature sensors, in particular, are highlighted for their crucial role in monitoring thermoregulation during physical activity. This article uses Allan’s Deviation, a time-domain analysis method, to investigate a selection of high-precision temperature sensors for their error and noise parameters. The results show the noise and error characteristics to steer the development of appropriate algorithms for filtering and fusion of the sensor data, which can increase their reliability. In addition, the paper presents the original experimental setup that allows for the investigation and characterization of integral temperature sensors.

articleTitle: Adaptive Kalman Filter with Probabilistic Gain Adjustment for Estimation of Satellite Position in the Presence of Measurement Faults
abstract: In this study, a probabilistic adaptive filtering technique is described for the Extended Kalman filter (EKF) algorithm, which is used to estimate Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite position, velocity, and clock bias using Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) distance measurements. The proposed probabilistic adaptive extended Kalman filter (pAEKF) algorithm is based on tracking normalized innovation sequences in the filter and calculating the probability of normal operation of the estimation system. The filter gain is adjusted based on this probability to maintain the filter’s tracking performance despite inaccurate measurements.

articleTitle: An Embedded Cellular Automata Algorithm for Infrared Object Detection
abstract: This work proposes and presents a cellular automata algorithm for infrared object detection and tracking. The algorithm’s application is aimed towards computationally limited edge computing sensory modules. Performed is a statistical evaluation of the algorithm’s noise resilience through a 3D histogram method. Proposed is a methodology for the optimal choice of the algorithm’s fine-tuning parameter values. The performance influence of applying low-pass Kernel filtering was evaluated and developed was a majority voting-based concurrent object mask-generating algorithm.

articleTitle: Using Digital Technologies in Mental Health Care
abstract: The purpose of this paper is related to using digital technologies to help users who experience various emotional problems such as depression, obsessive thoughts, anger, worry, suicidal ideation or harm to self and others. Users are provided with a platform in the form of a “chatbot”. But along with that, each user has a personalized plan with daily tasks, the progress of which is monitored and reported on the platform. Custom plans are set of commitments that the users must complete each day. These are beneficial actions that have been scientifically proven to help deal with the specific problem. These, as well as easy extensibility, are the main advantages of the proposed software solution.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing for Smart Agriculture Monitoring Pepper Crops
abstract: Remote sensing is an essential tool for modern agriculture, aiding in monitoring and managing crop health and productivity. This study focuses on assessing the ecological status of bell pepper crops (Capsicum annuum) using remote sensing techniques. It compares data from various sensors to identify the most effective tools for comprehensive crop assessment. The ultimate objective is to develop a reliable framework for remote monitoring, highlighting practical agricultural applications and improving the management and sustainability of vegetable crop production.

articleTitle: LTSpice-Based Stability Analysis of Boost DC-DC Converter for Application in Education of Power Electronics
abstract: The stability of power electronic devices is essential for their reliable and efficient operation. This aspect is particularly important in the design and operation of power converters such as DC-DC converters, inverters, etc. Stability analysis is critical to prevent instability that can lead to oscillations, poor performance, or system failure. Therefore, understanding and ensuring stability is a fundamental aspect in the design of power electronic devices In this article, we will look at methods for analyzing the stability of power electronic devices, with an emphasis on using LTspice to analyze the stability of a Boost DC-DC converter.

articleTitle: Remote Monitoring of the Atmosphere Air Quality
abstract: The authors of this article turn their attention to the problems associated with providing ambient air quality monitoring and the use of a remote uRADMonitor ® system in the training of students in engineering education. The authors’ idea is aimed at creating a combined training of students, by building skills and competencies, encouraging their active participation in capturing and analyzing data in real-time and using Matlab and Python software products for their processing.

articleTitle: Investigating the impact of temperature-humidity index on eye temperature in dairy cows using infrared thermography
abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the influence of temperature-humidity index (THI) on eye temperature in farmed dairy cows using infrared thermography. As THI increased, eye temperature increased. The correlation coefficient between the unduplicated ascending THI values and the arithmetic mean of the averaged eye temperatures was 0.584. The results show that as the THI value increases, the surface temperature of the eyes increases, which is a response to the heat load of the cows.

articleTitle: On automatic assessment of data generated by safety and security activities
abstract: Safety and security management prescribe specific requirements for their activities. Given the heavy reliance on documentation, assessing these activities is an exhausting and predominantly manual process. This typically makes the assessment time-intensive, subjective and non-scalable over different systems. This work leverages Semantic Web technology to make the data generated by these activities machine interpretable, thereby enabling its automatic assessment. For the assessment, safety and security requirements were translated to rules and then used to programmatically assess the activities’ compliance with the safety and security plans.

articleTitle: Moisture and Temperature Impact on the Delamination in ICs during Soldering
abstract: This article investigates the impact of temperature and humidity during the soldering process on integrated circuits (ICs). It presents a study on how external factors affect ICs using Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (SAM) in various scanning modes: A-scan, C-scan, B-scan, and a combined mode of C-scan + Relative Threshold Gate (RTG). The research focuses on how variations in temperature and humidity levels can influence the structural integrity and functionality of integrated circuits during soldering. The findings highlight the importance of controlling soldering conditions and underscore the necessity of employing methods like SAM for early detection and analysis of delaminations and defects, which are critical for ensuring the reliability and longevity of integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Speaker Identification Algorithm Using Biometric Speech Features in Deep Learning Neural Network
abstract: Speaker identification is based on the specific voice biometric characteristics comparison of two speaking persons to decide whether or not the voice of one called “unknown” is similar to the other called “known”. It is proposed in this article to develop speaker identification algorithm using Siamese deep learning neural network to compare the voice biometric characteristics of two speakers. The results achieved from algorithm implementation are presented to demonstrate the algorithm ability to speaker identification with sufficient precision.

articleTitle: Height Influence on Thermal Infrared Imaging of Large Objects with Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
abstract: Thermal infrared imaging using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has become a vital tool for monitoring large objects with relatively constant temperatures. This study investigates how the height at which UAVs operate influences the thermal infrared measurements of such objects. Despite the objects maintaining a stable temperature, the results reveal significant variations in thermal readings at different altitudes. Analysis shows that these discrepancies are closely linked to specific components of the radiation transfer equation, particularly atmospheric attenuation, surface emissivity, and emission from atmospheric volume. Understanding these tendencies is crucial for optimizing UAV-based thermal imaging applications, ensuring accurate data collection, and improving the reliability of temperature assessments from varying heights. This research provides insights into the complex interaction between measurement altitude and thermal infrared imaging accuracy, offering guidance for future UAV thermal imaging missions.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of UWB Transceivers for high-performance ranging
abstract: This study presents a comparative analysis of the latest chipsets in Ultra-Wideband (UWB) communications. It also details a comprehensive test harness developed to evaluate the precision of UWB integrated circuits (ICs). The criteria for comparison are thoroughly described, along with the rationale for their selection and the methodologies employed for measurement.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Teaching Students on Microcontrollers and Embedded Systems
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into education to enhance learning experiences and outcomes, particularly in engineering disciplines like microcontrollers and sensors. This paper explores the application of AI in supporting student learning in programming and understanding microcontrollers and sensors and embedded systems, focusing on personalized learning, interactive simulations, and real-time feedback mechanisms. By leveraging AI-driven tools, educators can provide tailored educational experiences that deepen student understanding and proficiency in these critical areas of engineering.

articleTitle: Improving the Area-Delay Tradeoff for Academic FPGA Architectures by Applying Rent’s Rule to Logic Block Modeling
abstract: This paper presents a study on the effect of using a smaller number of inputs in the FPGA logic block calculated according to a pre-compiled model based on Rent’s rule. This rule, when applied to the FPGA logic block with a logic block crossbar, allows for the reduction of the size of its multiplexers, thereby reducing its area and the delays in the switching circuits. The study uses a set of benchmark circuits, which are implemented in FPGA architectures with predefined parameters. The obtained results allow for comparing the architectures based on the total area and the critical path delays of the benchmark circuits.

articleTitle: Development and Initial Results of 3D Printed Models Using In-House Designed Device and Software
abstract: Three-dimensional printing is vital in medicine, particularly with the rise of fused filament fabrication (FFF) technology due to affordable and customizable 3D printers. This work aims to develop exclusive software for controlling an FFF 3D printer, enabling printing directly from image files. Using a Creality Ender-3 V3 SE and C#, the software reads imaging formats to generate G-code files. Successful tests printed seven objects from png or tiff files with $100 \%$ infill density. This method will be applied to create phantoms for X-ray imaging research.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Irrigation System for Smart Agriculture
abstract: The digitization of agricultural services through smart agriculture aims to enhance productivity and efficiency by utilizing sensors, intelligent devices, and communication protocols. Through the paper, we will try to clarify the importance of implementing smart agriculture for the efficient soil irrigation, and explore contemporary irrigation techniques. We focus on the implementation and testing of an IoT-based system for efficient soil irrigation within a controlled environment. The system monitors key parameters such as Total Dissolved Solids (TDS), pH levels, and soil moisture using sensors, with data processed by an Arduino Uno R4 Wi-Fi and transmitted to the Arduino Cloud. A real-time dashboard provides access to this data and alerts for timely interventions. This pilot study demonstrates the potential for scalable application, enabling informed decisions on irrigation and nutrient management to optimize crop productivity and sustainability. Our findings underscore the importance of smart agriculture technologies in addressing the challenges of modern farming.

articleTitle: Direct force control of the electromagnetic force of linear induction motor with end effects
abstract: This article investigates the possibility controlling of a linear induction motor with end effects. Linear induction motor is a special type of electrical machine with an open electromagnetic system and therefore has additional electromagnetic losses named end-effects. In literature has many methods for controlling an induction machine. This article proposes to explore the method known as Direct force control applied as a method for control of a linear induction motor. This method is suitable because gives a quick response to reference values.

articleTitle: A Study of the Influence of Phase-Shift Controlled LLC Converter Parameters on the Commutating Mechanisms in Continuous Conduction Mode
abstract: This paper aims to examine the impact of the ratio between parallel and series inductances of the resonant tank and the ratio between the switching and resonant frequencies on the switching mechanisms that occur during the output voltage regulation in a resonant LLC DC/DC converter when applying the phase-shift control method. Continuous conduction mode is considered. Based on the presented graphical results, recommendations are made regarding the selection of the inductance ratio to ensure a wide operating range of the converter under zero-voltage switching conditions.

articleTitle: Grasp planning and sign language gestures with 3D printed humanoid hand
abstract: This article presents sign language gestures application used for control of humanoid 3D printed hand with fingers, based on a modular principle. The 3D printed fingers are designed to be manufactured assembled, which facilitates the construction of the hand. All actuators, sensors, and electronic components, used in the hand control, are located in the palm. The sign language application provides good opportunities to test the dexterity and mechanical limitations of the developed humanoid hand. In addition to the sign language gestures program, a second application is created that allows hand control based on user input for each finger. The implemented software programs are described. Functional experiments are conducted and discussed.

articleTitle: Integrated single-stage column AFE for CMOS image sensor single slope ADCs
abstract: The paper presents analog and dual correlated double sampling (CDS) stages employed in single-slope analog-to-digital converters (SS-ADC). The converter front-end comprises a single operational amplifier with switch-capacitor periphery circuitry. The compact architecture can perform operations such as CDS, auto-zeroing, amplification with programmable gain (PGA), and comparison that are combined as analog front end (AFE). Both CDS implementations are described in a system that uses only analog CDS for high-speed imagers and another structure for low-noise CIS applications. Due to the constantly increasing resolution of CMOS image sensors, the demand for high-integrity column-parallel ADC requires compact design solutions. The proposed concept is design-completed and simulated data supports the system validity provided along.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Combined High-pass and Notch Filter
abstract: This article presents a FPGA implementation of a combined filter for the simultaneous removal of power line interference and low-frequency drift from ECG signals. The proposed combined filter design is based upon the previously described in [4] model, which is a combination of several filters, and which has zeros at the power line and low-band drift frequencies. A procedure is used which generates a set of filter coefficients, and by means of a performed analytical procedure, the coefficients were converted to a 10-bit value. Synthesized is a structure for direct FPGA implementation. MATLAB and FPGA parallel tests were carried out both with artificial and real ECG signals with a present interference. The results show that there is an observable reduction in the baseline drift and an above -60dB suppression of power line interference.

articleTitle: Universal digital architecture with the ability to learn behavior based on self-generated questions
abstract: The article describes a digital system based on a new component called intelligent neuron, which is able to formulate a question and generate behavior. The system is subject to an external configurator of the horizontal and vertical connections between the intelligent neurons and an external teacher to answer all the neurons questions.

articleTitle: Harmonic Analysis of Transistor Resonance Inverter
abstract: Harmonic analysis is a method of examining the frequency components in signals generated by electronic devices such as resonant inverters. It allows to determine and quantify the harmonics (multipliers of the fundamental frequency) that may occur during inverter operation. This is particularly important because these harmonics can cause unwanted effects such as interference, overheating, efficiency losses and other problems in the system. Harmonic analysis is a critical tool for engineers in the design and optimization of resonant inverters. It helps ensure high efficiency, reliability and standards compliance while helping to ensure the performance of power electronic devices.

articleTitle: Intelligent System for Conducting Experiments with DC/DC Converters
abstract: The paper presents an automated system with application in power electronics for $D C / D C$ converter efficiency measurements. The structure and the main functions of the virtual instrument are presented along with sample test measurements. Main features include the plotting in real time of the obtained results, ability to react in critical situations via the GUI using safety features buttons, faster and flexible measurements set-up and multi-platform capability, due to the fact that open-source software is used.

articleTitle: Automated Research of Flexible Sensing Structures
abstract: In recent years, with the development of concepts such as the Internet of Things and Wearable electronics, the use of sensor structures on flexible substrates has become increasingly prevalent. Since these structures are typically printed in various shapes, on different substrates, and with exotic inks, there is no established mathematical model for their behavior. This necessitates the use of measured results to derive empirical dependencies. In the present article, an approach is proposed for using virtual measurement instruments to automate the research process.

articleTitle: Simulation Environment for the Evaluation of LiDAR Odometry Algorithms
abstract: This study focused on enhancing odometry estimation for self-driving cars using LiDAR-based sensor technology. The project involves integrating LiDAR sensors into the car’s sensor suite, which generates detailed 3D point clouds of the environment. This integration can be useful when gaps-based odometry estimation is not accurate enough. These point clouds are then used to accurately estimate the vehicle’s movement and position using learning-based and model-based odometry estimation methods.

articleTitle: High-power isolated hybrid solar inverter
abstract: The increasing percentage of renewable energy in the European Union leads to an increasingly vital question of energy storage. Proposing a highly efficient hybrid power inverter with galvanic isolation between the battery and the grid is the main purpose of this paper. The proposed circuit is first analyzed and then simulation for the different modes of operation and experimental verification of its efficiency in both directions of energy transfer are given.

articleTitle: Analysis of the retention process of business customers in the Telecom industry
abstract: The telecommunications industry is a dynamic and fast-growing sector in which technological innovation occurs quickly. The industry is one of the most competitive on a global scale, where companies are constantly striving to increase their number of customers. Despite the high level of competition, the telecommunications industry faces a significant churn rate. To deal with this challenging aspect of the industry it is essential that company management model and implement effective processes for customer service. The business customer retention process is a key process in the customer service departments of telecommunications companies. The process requires in-depth analysis related to predicting customers’ intent to withdraw and initiating actions focused on retention using defensive trading strategies. This paper offers a process model, an analysis of process strengths and weaknesses, and an opportunity to improve the process by using technological solutions based on the latest research in artificial intelligence and machine learning.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of the Junction Formation Mechanisms of the Boron on Silicon Junction
abstract: Photodiodes based on the Boron on Silicon junction (B-Si) show excellent responsivity to DUV and VUV photons, radiation hardness, and impressive electrical characteristics. However, the proposed models describing the junction formation mechanism do not sufficiently predict the junction’s properties. We analyze two previously proposed models: the ultra-shallow p-n junction model and the charge transfer heterojunction model. We additionally apply the Schottky-Mott theory, a semiconductor-metal heterojunction model. Both the commonalities and incompatibilities between these models are discussed.

articleTitle: Investigation of Linear Discrete Time-Invariant Systems Models Using MATLAB and Signal Processing Toolbox
abstract: The paper exposes a brief overview of existing models of linear, discrete, and time-invariant systems and then offers a guide to utilizing these models in MATLAB. Embedded functions for modeling in MATLAB and Signal Processing Toolbox and examples for transforming from one model to another are given. The “Digital Signal Processing” course for “Information and Communication Technologies” and “Internet and Mobile Communications” bachelor students incorporates these issues into its teaching methods. An attractive way of presenting the material for easier adoption by students is proposed in the paper.

articleTitle: Combined Footprint - Results and Conclusions: Review
abstract: The article reviews the development of a new soldering method with the application of a solder paste with a combined footprint, which allows to ensure optimal individual soldering of each solder joint in the electronic module in a single soldering process (reflow soldering). The achievements of the research of the method over time, as well as the work of many researchers on improving soldering by adding various materials to the solder - metals, oxides, ceramics, nanomaterials and others - are reviewed. In the conclusions, it is emphasized that by using the obtained results and by means of analysis with statistical methods and machine learning, a software module can be created in the design softwares to determine the individual conditions for optimal soldering of each solder joint in the designed electronic module and this information can be loaded directly for execution by production machines (Jet printers).

articleTitle: Q-adaptive AKF for Estimation of UAV dynamics in the Case of Biased Process Noise
abstract: In this study a covariance matching-based adaptive Kalman filter (AKF) with Q-adaptation is examined. Influence of the process noise bias type system changes to the prediction, estimation and state correction sequence of Kalman filter ($\mathbf{K F}$) is investigated. It is proved that the bias type process noise change may be converted to the mean square of state correction sequence of KF and such type of changes can be compensatd using the covarince matching techniques.

articleTitle: Wi-Fi HaLow Wildfire Sound Detector
abstract: The expanding severity and occurrences of wildfires has led researchers in search for new technologies and applying cutting-edge solutions for the early detection of such fire hazards. Within this work we propose a Wi-Fi HaLow wildfire sound detector. Described are the spectral specifics of forest fire noise, the Wi-Fi HaLow standard and its advantages. The prototyped system was subjected to tests capturing real sound data from fire and non-fire events and distinguishing between them by means of sonogram analysis.

articleTitle: Impact of Multi-Threading on All-SMT Solving
abstract: Configurable software architectures enhance software development by reusing common functionalities. Testing these architectures involves All-Solution Satisfiability Modulo Theories (All-SMT) solving, which can be computationally intensive. This paper introduces a multi-threaded approach to reduce All-SMT execution time. The impact of going multithreaded applied to multiple All-SMT strategies is analyzed. Experiments show that gain is negligible when an SMT problem is small. However, once an SMT problem becomes complex, up to 6x and higher speedups can be achieved.

articleTitle: Electronic System for Remote Control of Foundry Furnace
abstract: An IoT-based electronic system allowing manual and remote control of a 9 kW foundry furnace has been developed. In the first case, the control is carried out through a rotary encoder, and in the second one - through an Internet browser, smartphone, or computer. The results of the measured temperatures and the set limits for turning the furnace on and off are displayed on an LED display, smartphone, or computer. The electronic control system of the foundry furnace enables software processing of information, automatic measurement, and real-time control. The main objective is to control the temperature ranges to obtain quality foundries, which would lead to a reduction in the scrap of the finished products. The results of the experimental studies carried out with the developed electronic system show that for the staged insertion of aluminum, the time required to reach the optimum casting temperature is approximately two hours.

articleTitle: Modelling Distribution of Fire in Apartments: Case Study in Bulgaria
abstract: Fires in residential buildings are one of the great problems of mankind. Numerical modelling of a fire in an apartment with and without a corridor was done in the work. Results are presented for main parameters during the development of the fire in both cases and at different time intervals - 120s, 300s, $475 \mathrm{~s}, 600 \mathrm{~s}$ and 674 s. Conclusions have been made that can be of use to firefighting services in buildings.

articleTitle: A System for Uninterrupted Diagnostic Diesel Generator Engine
abstract: The preventive diagnostic became more and more important in real maintenance of ship diesel engines especially in Power Management System. In this issue only some are shown outcomes of research works in the field of marine engine diagnostics. A set up of additional encoder, capturing controller and calculating program is used to establish a new system for sensing deviations in the engine crankshaft rotational speed. So it solve the traditional problem with the early finding of an engine performance deviation in the initial stage of its development.

articleTitle: Customer Segmentation and Customer Churn Analysis in Telecommunications Industry
abstract: In this study, it is aimed to develop a customer segmentation model with the help of the data mining method, make the necessary classification and conduct customer loss analysis accordingly, based on large-scale customer data of the company operating in the telecommunications sector. The usability of this software model has been tested in the company operating in the telecommunications industry. In this context, it has been tried to contribute to the establishment of a system suitable for the company’s structure in the sector and to increase its competitiveness with rival companies and raise it to a higher level.

articleTitle: Generative Audio Steganography Algorithm
abstract: Steganography methods hide information in video or audio records. The main disadvantage is the reduced resistance to hidden information disclosure using today effective and fast stenographic analysis. The algorithm proposed in this article is based on generative adversarial neural networks to direct transformation of the input audio information as steganography data. The algorithm is tested as corresponding program application and the examination of created generative steganography audio data confirm the achieved high resistance to unauthorized recovering.

articleTitle: A Sustainable Approach to Improve Soil Health. A Case Study for Western Bulgaria
abstract: The study investigates the effects of biochar, produced from alfalfa at $400^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $600^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, on soil health in Western Bulgaria. Eleven soil samples were analyzed for $\mathbf{p H}$, nitrate, phosphate, and potassium levels before and after biochar application. Results indicated that biochar improved phosphorus and potassium levels, essential for crop growth, while maintaining stable nitrate content, thus promoting sustainable agriculture. The research highlights biochar’s potential to enhance soil fertility, reduce chemical fertilizer use, and support environmentally friendly farming practices, contributing to better soil management and carbon sequestration efforts.

articleTitle: Approaches to Improving the Visualization Accuracy of the Technology of Integrating Functional Near-infrared Spectroscopy with the Brain-computer Interface
abstract: The article provides a comparative analysis of existing approaches aimed at improving the accuracy of visualization using functional near-infrared spectroscopy when integrated with the brain-computer interface. Various aspects of functional near-infrared spectroscopy data are being investigated, including signal acquisition, preprocessing, and feature extraction. A comparative analysis of signal filtering technologies at the preprocessing stage and signal processing methods at the feature extraction stage is carried out. The features of the application of such methods as the discrete Fourier transform, the wavelet transform, and the HilbertHuang transform for data processing are presented.

articleTitle: Recognition of Human Actions in an Object Environment in Videos
abstract: In this work recognition of human actions of daily life is studied. Such actions take place in an environment involving various objects. The performance depends on hyper-parameters. High-level 3D primitives are considered using human skeleton and Bayesian approach is applied for online recognition. A fusion mechanism is involved to optimize the parameters and to improve the performance. The approach shows interesting results especially regarding imbalanced data and under-represented classes in datasets.

articleTitle: Application of Open-Source Software in Analog and Mixed-signal Circuits Education
abstract: The article examines the applicability of modern open-source software products in the education of students in courses related to analysis and design of analog and mixed-signal circuits. The study considers an interactive demonstration of the operational principle of basic analog and mixed-signal circuits, including possibilities for solving specific optimization tasks through open-source software products. The considered possibilities are confirmed by specific practical educational examples.

articleTitle: Driver physiological parameters monitoring–initial study in real-road driving
abstract: Among the human factors which contribute to road accidents and crashes special attention deserve medical conditions, drowsiness and fatigue. Monitoring the physiological parameters of the vehicle driver in a real-road driving is a very challenging task, as the signals from biomedical sensors are often distorted by noises, motion artefacts and vibrations inside the car. In this paper a system for monitoring a driver’s physiological signals from Electrocardiogram (ECG), Respiratory Rate (RR), Electrodermal Activity (EDA) and Photoplethysmography (PPG) sensors is presented. The signals are collected in real driving scenarios on different road types and various locations of sensing electrodes in order to determine their appropriate placement for obtaining high quality signals. The results show that placing the ECG sensor electrodes below the chest is preferable because the signal is less affected by motion artefacts, vibration and noise. Also, better quality signals are obtained when the belt with an integrated RR sensor is located in close proximity to the level of diaphragm, EDA electrodes are placed on the right hand palm and PPG sensor is attached to the earlobe.

articleTitle: Legal Framework of Automated Vehicles: Comparative Analysis and Proposals for Regulation in Bulgaria
abstract: Adequate legal regulation is an important factor for companies to choose the location to make business in the field of development, testing and use of new technologies in the automotive sector. Many countries worldwide (USA, France, Germany, UK, Netherlands, etc.) have already adopted automated vehicles regulations. The paper offers a brief comparative analysis of legal framework of testing and use of automated vehicles in different jurisdictions. Based on the analysis, conclusions and proposals are made regarding the elaboration of automated vehicles regulation in Bulgaria.

articleTitle: Cryptocurrency – a curious event in modern day society
abstract: Cryptocurrency is still a relatively new invention, but it has already impacted the everyday life of a percentage of people, be it good or bad. But are cryptocurrencies a risk, an opportunity or something else? Are they limited to the individual or can they have a wider impact? The goal of this article is to try and answer these questions and give a broad analysis of the different interactions between cryptocurrency and different aspect of human life.

articleTitle: The Utility of Evolutionary and Genetic Computing in Battery Modeling
abstract: Evolutionary Computing and Genetic Algorithms have gained popularity as a Machine Learning technique for multi-objective optimization. Within this work we investigate their various application in data-driven battery modeling. Presented are specifics regarding the underlying mechanisms governing battery degradation and the main numerical health metrics. Discussed is the topic of physics-based constriction of Machine Learning models and methods for inference acceleration.

articleTitle: Anomaly-Based Intrusion Detection System Design Using Machine Learning Methods
abstract: In this study, studies on intrusion detection systems have been meticulously examined and an example model of the intrusion detection system has been created. The UNSW-NB15 data set used in this process was subjected to training and testing stages with machine learning methods such as Logistic Regression, K-nearest Neighbor Algorithm, Support Vector Machines, Naive Bayes, Decision Tree and Random Forest Algorithm. By applying machine learning methods to the data used in the training phase, normal network traffic was taught and a reference model was created with this information.
